# HandicapBathtubs.com

> Guides to bathing with a mobility disability: wheelchair transfer tubs and transfer technique, the 2010 ADA Standards for bathtubs (sections 607, 608, 609, 610), what applies in private homes, caregiver-assisted bathing, public funding (VA HISA, SAH, SHA, Medicaid waivers, vocational rehabilitation) and U.S. Census disability data. Operated by Aging Safely Baths, a family-owned company selling and installing accessible tubs and showers since 2012.

Contact: 1-888-779-2284, sales@agingsafelybaths.com. Installation in many U.S. areas; supply-only shipping to the U.S. and Canada. Prices are quoted individually and are not published on this site. Main company site: https://www.agingsafelybaths.com/

## Guides
- [Handicap bathtubs that work from a wheelchair](https://handicapbathtubs.com/): Wheelchair transfer tubs, exact ADA tub measurements, caregiver transfers and VA and Medicaid funding, from Aging Safely Baths. Call 1-888-779-2284.
- [Wheelchair transfer tubs and safe transfer technique](https://handicapbathtubs.com/wheelchair-transfer-tubs/): How wheelchair transfer tubs work, who they suit, how to measure, and step-by-step sliding, stand-pivot and lift transfers based on MedlinePlus guidance.
- [ADA bathtub requirements, measured: sections 607, 608 and 610](https://handicapbathtubs.com/ada-bathtub-requirements/): Exact 2010 ADA bathtub rules: 30-inch clearance, seats 17 to 19 inches high, grab bars 33 to 36 inches, a 59-inch hand shower hose and a 120°F cap.
- [ADA vs residential bathrooms: which rules apply in your home?](https://handicapbathtubs.com/ada-vs-residential-bathrooms/): The ADA does not cover a private home bathroom. Here is what the Fair Housing Act, Section 504 and local codes require, and which ADA numbers to borrow.
- [Caregiver-assisted bathing for a person with a mobility disability](https://handicapbathtubs.com/caregiver-assisted-bathing/): How to help a person with a mobility disability bathe without lifting them: transfer methods, a step-by-step routine and tub features that protect the helper.
- [Paying for a handicap bathtub with a disability: VA, Medicaid and vocational rehab](https://handicapbathtubs.com/blog-ways-to-pay-for-a-handicap-bathtub.html): VA HISA, SAH and SHA amounts for 2026, Medicaid waiver home modifications, vocational rehab, Medicare limits and tax rules for an accessible tub, with sources.
- [How to plan a wheelchair accessible bathtub layout](https://handicapbathtubs.com/blog-wheelchair-accessible-bathtub-layouts.html): Plan a wheelchair accessible bathtub layout around the transfer: door side, clear floor, turning space, plumbing and caregiver room, with ADA measurements.
- [Handicap bathtubs vs standard tubs for people with mobility disabilities](https://handicapbathtubs.com/blog-handicap-vs-standard-bathtubs.html): How a standard tub, a walk-in tub and a wheelchair transfer tub compare for people with mobility disabilities, including transfer benches and caregiver help.
- [VA SAH and SHA grants for an accessible bathroom: 2026 amounts and the bathroom rules](https://handicapbathtubs.com/va-sah-sha-bathroom-requirements/): FY 2026 VA SAH ($126,526), SHA ($25,350) and TRA amounts, who qualifies, and the SAH primary bathroom minimums from VA Pamphlet 26-13 (roll-in shower 48 x 48 in, 36 in opening, 36 in door, 5 ft turning space), with a plan checker and grant finder.
- [Bathing after a spinal cord injury: equipment and bathroom setup by hand function](https://handicapbathtubs.com/bathing-after-spinal-cord-injury/): Shower commode chairs, tub transfer benches, transfer and reclining tubs and roll-in shower sizes matched to hand function, with burn and skin safety steps from rehabilitation guides, plus a setup planner.

## Data
- [Disability in the U.S. by age and state: Census data, charted](https://handicapbathtubs.com/disability-statistics/): 42.7 million Americans report a disability, and 57.9% are under 65. Census ACS 2019–2023 data by age and state, charted, with a full state table.

## Other
- [Privacy note](https://handicapbathtubs.com/privacy/): What HandicapBathtubs.com does with the details you send through its quote form, who receives them, and how to ask for them to be deleted.
